newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey prepares draft to improve tax law.
newsitem.headline: Turkey prepares draft to improve tax law.

text.p: Turkey's finance ministry on Thursday presented a draft law to parliament which envisages improvements in tax collection and give tax advantages to foreign-partnered joint ventures, parliament officials said.

The law will make it possible "to obtain considerable results if approved by parliament," said Finance Minister Abdullatif Sener after presenting the draft law. It was not immediately known when parliament will vote on the draft.
"It will provide for a fair tax distribution, eliminate gaps stemming from tax losses and leakages, and enhance the models designed to develop the eceonomic and technology," Sener told parliament.
The draft, which brings changes to the Tax Law No. 213 and Income Tax No. 193, envisages the production of documents that will enable cash flows and taxable items, he said.

It will also enable joint ventures to revaluate their assets in line with inflation through a revaluation rate announced by the government at the beginning of every year, reducing their taxable assests.

The law will especially boost investments under the build-operate-transfer (BOT) scheme, which Turkey devised in 1980s to build big energy, tourism and other infrastructure projects by joint ventures.

The new law will also enable a "revaluation of securities for a fair tax system through on a seasonal basis," Sener said. Under the present system the buy price of securities are taken as the basis for taxation.
